prs.title: fix(link): resolve a relative path from the current directory
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Related to pnpm/pnpm#17475.

pnpm v12 resolved a relative `pnpm link <dir>` against the directory of the nearest `package.json`, not the directory the command runs in. In a folder without a `package.json`, such as a workspace's `packages` folder, `pnpm link .` therefore linked the workspace root into itself. It wrote `"<root-name>": "link:"` to the root `package.json` and `<root-name>: link:.` to the overrides. pnpm v11 resolves the path against the current directory. v12 now does the same.

Context from #17475: the reporter's error reproduces exactly with pnpm 11.13.1 on the reporter's repository (mcp-use at 8d8034e, Windows, under a Hebrew-named profile path):

1. Run `pnpm link .` in `libraries/typescript/packages`, which has no `package.json`. 11.13.1 writes `".": "link:packages"` to the root `package.json` and `.: link:packages` to the overrides, then fails with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SELECTOR`.
2. Remove only the override. `pnpm build:mcp-use` then prints the reporter's output verbatim: `✓ Lockfile passes supply-chain policies (verified …)`, then `[ERR_PNPM_INVALID_DEPENDENCY_NAME] The current package contains a dependency with an invalid name: "."`.

On main, v11 (#17535) refuses step 1 without changing either file. v12 resolved `.` against the root, so it never produced `"."`, but it linked the wrong project. This PR fixes that.

Verified by hand with a v12 binary built from main, in the reporter's repository. `pnpm link .` in `packages` wrote the self-link bef

fix: ignore the version of a lone project in the dependency-status check
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Bumping only the `version` of a single-project repository made `verifyDepsBeforeRun` report "The workspace structure has changed since last install" and spawn an install before the script. In pnpm v12 the install fast path re-resolved too.

The dependency-status check compares each recorded project's name and version with its manifest. A project's version decides only how *other* workspace projects' dependencies resolve to it, so the version is now compared only when the workspace has more than one project, or when `linkWorkspacePackages` is `deep` (a transitive dependency may then resolve to the lone project). The name, the project set, and every other check stay as they were. Multi-project workspaces keep the strict comparison: a dependent's `workspace:^1` or a linked range can stop matching after a bump.

Fixed in both stacks:

- v12: `project_structure_matches` in `pnpm/crates/package-manager/src/optimistic_repeat_install/settle.rs` (shared by the run gate, the install fast path, and the relocation check). It now takes the config to read `linkWorkspacePackages`.
- v11: `findWorkspaceStructureIssue` in `pnpm11/deps/status`. v11 reaches this check only when a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` exists, as in the issue's repro.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17560

### Verification

- The issue's repro on a fixed v12 debug build: the `warn` run prints no warning, the default run starts no install.
- New Rust unit tests: a lone project's bump passes both the install fast path and the run ga

Implements steps 1–3 of the [SQL metadata storage RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-sql-metadata-storage.md) and the parts of its step 4 conformance suite that apply to an embedded backend. Part of pnpm/tasks#244. This is the base of a stack: atomic workspace publication builds on it.

fix(link): add the link: dependency to the current project in v11
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

In a workspace, v11 `pnpm link <dir>` added the `link:` dependency to the workspace root's `package.json` instead of the project where the command ran. The link was then created only in the root's `node_modules`. This contradicts the docs ("a link to `bar` will be created in `foo/node_modules/bar`") and v12, which adds the dependency to the current project. Found while investigating pnpm/pnpm#17475.

Running `pnpm link ../../../bar` from `packages/foo`, where `foo` doesn't depend on `bar` yet:

| | Root `package.json` | `packages/foo/package.json` | Override | Link created in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v11 before | `"bar": "link:../bar"` | unchanged | `bar: link:../bar` | root `node_modules` only |
| v11 after / v12 | unchanged | `"bar": "link:../../../bar"` | `bar: link:../bar` | `foo/node_modules` only |

Running from a folder inside the workspace that has no `package.json`, such as `packages/`, still falls back to the root project, as in v12. I checked both cases end to end with the rebuilt bundle.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
In a workspace, v11 `pnpm link <dir>` added the `link:` dependency to the
workspace root's package.json instead of the project where the command
ran. That is a leftover from pnpm/pnpm#8653, which moved the write to the
root manifest because the overrides lived in its `pnpm.overrides` field.
When pnpm/pnpm#9365 moved overrides to pnpm-workspace.yaml, the dependency
kept going to the root. The docs and v12 add it to the current project.

prs.author: zkochan

## Summary

Implements a subset of the [atomic workspace publication RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-atomic-workspace-publication.md) on top of the SQLite metadata store. Part of pnpm/tasks#244. Builds on the SQLite metadata store from pnpm/pnpm#17551, now on main.

Everything here applies when `metadata: { backend: sqlite }` is set. The documents backend keeps the journaled path unchanged.

### What it covers

- **One SQL commit path for publishing.** `commit_publishes` and the single and batch publish handlers commit every staged document of a request in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. That transaction advances the org's catalog generation once (RFC Implementation step 2, for publishing). Archives are promoted before the transaction. A slot another writer holds with different bytes fails the whole request with `409` before any metadata commits, so the "partial release on a lost race" outcome of the journal is gone for SQLite. prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Part of pnpm/tasks#244. First of two stacked PRs with the release-record trust primitives from the [release records RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-release-records.md) (the "Transparency log" section).

This adds `pnpm-transparency-log`, a standalone crate for pnpr and pnpm. It has the C2SP formats the RFC uses (the ones Go's checksum database uses):

- **Keys** ([signed-note](https://c2sp.org/signed-note)): verifier keys written `<name>+<key hash>+<key>` (lowercase key hash; names follow tlog-cosignature: at most 255 bytes, no spaces, `+`, or control characters), `NoteSigner` for log signatures, and `Cosigner` for Ed25519 checkpoint cosignatures (`cosignature/v1`, [tlog-cosignature](https://c2sp.org/tlog-cosignature)).
- **Checkpoints** ([tlog-checkpoint](https://c2sp.org/tlog-checkpoint)): `sign_checkpoint`, `add_signatures`, and `CheckpointPolicy::verify`. Verification needs the log key threshold and the witness quorum, each counted over distinct keys in the policy set (a repeated signature line counts once), with log keys of signed-note type `0x01` and witness keys of type `0x04`. A key set cannot list one public key under two names, and a witness cannot reuse a log key, since an Ed25519 cosignature does not commit to the cosigner name. It ignores unknown signers and rejects a bad signature from a named key. A policy with no witnesses (a private registry) is allowed.
- **Tiles** ([tlog-tiles](https://c2sp.org/tlog-tiles)): `TilePath`

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements the pnpr side of the [release notes RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-release-notes.md): Implementation step 1 and most of step 2, for npm routes. Part of pnpm/tasks#244. Builds on the SQLite metadata store (pnpm/pnpm#17551) and atomic publication (pnpm/pnpm#17553), both now on main.

Everything here applies when `metadata: { backend: sqlite }` is set. Without it, a publish that carries notes is refused with `400`.

### What it covers

- **Storage (step 1).** Two new tables. `notes` is keyed by catalog and subject: a package version (ecosystem, name, version) or a publication id. It stores the text (`NULL` once deleted), modification time, principal, and the digest of the text the subject was published with. `note_history` is insert-only and keeps every change with the text it replaced, so an edit or deletion can be restored. A note is never created ahead of its subject: an unknown version or publication answers `404`.

prs.title: fix(deploy): keep project links whose target is missing in the source
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm deploy` dropped (v12) or failed with ENOENT on (v11) a project symlink whose target is missing in the source, such as a Next.js `.next/node_modules` alias in a build restored without its `node_modules`. Under deploy's `Internal` symlink policy such a link is now kept as a directory link with its original text, so it resolves to the dependency deploy installs in the output.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17571

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`pnpm deploy` copies the project with the `Internal` symlink policy, which
keeps a directory link whose target is left out of the copy. A link whose
target is missing in the source, such as a Next.js alias into a
`node_modules` that a restored build artifact no longer has, did not count
as a directory link. pnpm v12 dropped it silently, and pnpm v11 fell
through to copying the link as a file and failed with ENOENT.

Under `Internal`, a link whose target is missing is now recreated as a
directory link with its original text. The deploy then installs the target,
so the link resolves inside the output. A directory link is used because
on Windows a junction is the only link a process without the symlink
privilege can create, and the usual missing target is a package directory.
Links that escape the package root are still refused.

The v11 importer now also omits a dangling link under the `imported`
policy, matching v12, where it used to fail copying it.

The deploy e2e tests in both stacks run the existing link scenario a second
time afte
…(truncated)

## Summary

Adds the native Git, Git-hosted tarball, and binary fetchers to the `fetchers` argument of pnpmfile custom fetchers in pnpm v12, covering [pnpm/tasks#191](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

A result from one of these fetchers must be returned unchanged, like the existing `localTarball`, `remoteTarball`, and `directory` results. The Git callback rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` when the lockfile pins an archive integrity, as the directory callback does, and the binary callback rejects an archive whose integrity does not match the locked one.

```text

fetchers.git, and fetchers.binary. Each callback runs pacquet's own
fetcher and records the files it produced; a hook may return only a
files map that one of these callbacks verified, matched path for path.

materialization pass.

archive whose integrity does not match the locked one, so a hook cannot
swap a locked package's content. Like the tarball callbacks, they
reject ignoreFilePattern and appendManifest.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fourth of the SQL metadata adapter stack (pnpm/tasks#244, design in pnpm/rfcs#66 "Shared deployments"). Builds on pnpm/pnpm#17577, pnpm/pnpm#17578 and pnpm/pnpm#17580, now merged.

Adds the libSQL metadata adapter, so several pnpr instances share one metadata database such as Turso. The schema and queries are the same as for SQLite.

```yaml
s3:
  bucket: my-pnpr-packages      # archives stay in object storage
metadata:
  url: libsql://my-db.turso.io  # or http(s):// for a self-hosted sqld
  authToken: ${TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN}
  replicaPath: ./metadata-replica.db
  syncInterval: 10s
```

**Where each read goes.** The shared layer decides freshness, and the adapter decides the source:

| Read | Freshness | libSQL source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read-for-update (CAS), recorded outcome of a retried publish, catalog generation | `Current` | primary |
| authorization (`is_package_owner`, which now reads for update) | `Current` | primary |
| package views, listings, publications, notes, tag history | `Bounded` | replica, if its last sync is within `syncInterval` and no write of this process came after it; else sync, else primary |
| a client's minimum generation (`Storage::read_hosted_package_view_at_least`) | `AtLeast(g)` | replica once it reaches `g` (synced on demand), else primary |

A replica read runs in one `BEGIN READONLY` transaction, which keeps it on the replica; a plain `BEGIN` on a replica connection goes to the primary. Every write of this process marks the repl

prs.author: kiyors
prs.body:
> **Note**: The overall code in this pull request was written by AI and heavily reviewed, iterated on, and thoroughly tested end-to-end by a person in live workspaces and via automated test suites.

## Summary

Enhances the pnpm v12 agent skills system with three major capabilities:

1. **Selective Skill Approval (`permissions.<pkg>.skills: [...]`)**:
   - When an approved package ships more than one skill, `pnpm approve` presents an interactive checklist allowing users to approve specific skills or all of them.
   - Approvals are recorded as a list in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
     ```yaml
     permissions:
       drizzle-kit:
         skills: [guide, migrate]
     ```

## Summary

First PR of the "archive upload by integrity" stack, the upload half of [atomic workspace publication](pnpr/text/0000-atomic-workspace-publication.md#prepare-and-commit) ("Archives are uploaded one at a time, addressed by their integrity, before the commit request"). Part of pnpm/tasks#244. Based on `main`.

- `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/artifacts/blob?integrity=<sha512-…>` **without an owner** stages one release archive for the calling account. `HEAD` on the same URL says whether it is staged, with its size. Only a complete archive answers `HEAD` or can be claimed. A failed upload gives its reservation back; one that stopped stops counting after an hour.

## Summary

Third PR of the release-records stack; it builds on #17601, now merged. It implements the rest of step 1 of the [release records RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-release-records.md#transparency-log): sequence each record's log entry in the acceptance transaction, and integrate the sequenced entries into a C2SP tiled log whose tiles and checkpoints live in blob storage.

- **Sequencing.** A record's entry (`pnpr-log-entry/1`: identity, revision, profile, digest, built by `pnpm-release-record`) is appended to a new insert-only `log_entries` table. This happens in the same transaction that accepts the version, at the log's next index, and the record row keeps that index. A version can't be accepted without its entry, and an entry can't be logged without its version. Removing a version keeps its entry, because a log only grows.
- **Integration.** `Storage::integrate_log` reads the entries the latest checkpoint doesn't cover yet. It writes the hash tiles and entry bundles they add, using `pnpm-transparency-log`'s `integrate`, then signs and writes a checkpoint of the larger tree. ## Summary

Fourth PR of the release-records stack; it sits on #17602. It serves what the [release records RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-release-records.md#client-protocol) asks a registry to serve for its log, with the RFC's disclosure rules.

- **`<base>/-/log/checkpoint`, `<base>/-/log/tile/<L>/<N>[.p/<W>]`, `<base>/-/log/tile/entries/<N>[.p/<W>]`.** A registry address serves the log of the one hosted organization it reaches; a registry that reaches none or several serves none.

  - Entry bundles name every logged package, so only a caller who may read every package of the organization (by `all_access_admit`, or a registry admin) gets them. Anyone else gets the same 404 for every bundle, whatever it holds.
  - Tiles are cached forever and the checkpoint is `no-cache`. Everything is `private, no-store` when some package is closed to anonymous callers, or when reached through a named registry, as every `/~<name>/` response is.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fifth PR of the release-records stack; it sits on #17603. It implements the acceptance half of the [release records RFC's statements](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-release-records.md#statements-in-toto-in-dsse) (implementation step 2).

- **Configuration.** `releaseRecords.statementSigningKey` takes a signed-note private key, with env substitution enforced as for other secrets. Each DSSE signature's `keyid` is the key's `<name>+<key hash>`, as the RFC asks.
- **The statement.** With the key set, a record's evidence (`<name>/<version>+r<revision>/evidence`) lists the registry's acceptance statement. It's an in-toto Statement about the record, by its digest and PURL, with predicate type `https://pnpm.io/pnpr/acceptance/v1` and `{ "interpretation": <profile> }`. It's built and signed by `pnpm-release-record` (`Statement::about`, `Statement::sign`).
- **Signed on read.** The statement is signed each time the evidence is read, from the record the metadata store accepted, so nothing new is stored.
  - Ed25519 is deterministic, so one key always signs the same envelope.
  - A key rotation re-signs every statement without a migration.
  - After a compromise, every statement is regenerated from the authoritative SQL record, never from an envelope the old key signed. That's what the RFC asks for.

Phase 1 of pnpm/tasks#256: the repeat-install fast path should decide "Already up to date" without reading any `package.json` whose stat is unchanged. Today it reads and parses every project manifest on every run.

A filtered write carries the records of the projects it leaves out, the same way it carries their digests, but only a record whose stat was trusted when it was recorded.

`pnpm publish -r --batch` to a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`:

1. sends `HEAD <registry>/-/pnpr/v0/artifacts/blob?integrity=<sha512-…>` for each package's archive, and skips the ones the registry holds staged;

`pnpm store add` now accepts package tarballs downloaded some other way, and prepares the store so `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` can install the registry packages they contain:

pnpm store add ./tarballs/*.tgz

This is what sandboxed builders such as flatpak-builder and Nix need. They download every source ahead of time with a hash they verify, then build without network access. ## Summary

Phase 3 of pnpm/tasks#256. With `verifyDepsBeforeRun` set, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` in an up-to-date workspace no longer read the `package.json` of each project whose file did not change since the last install.

pnpm/pnpm#17637 gave the install fast path a first attempt on manifests rebuilt from the workspace state's records. The verify-deps gate still parsed every project manifest on each gated command. It now makes the same attempt when one lockfile covers the workspace and the state holds manifest records:

1. It lists the project directories without reading them.
2. It rebuilds a stand-in for each manifest whose recorded stat still holds and is trusted.
3. It runs the gate's own check on the stand-ins.

Only an up-to-date verdict from the stand-ins stands. Any other verdict, or a project without a usable record, sends the gate to the check on the manifest files. That check reads the projects already listed, so whatever the gate reports as outdated comes from the files. The check on stand-ins never writes, as in pnpm/pnpm#17637.

Dedicated per-project lockfiles keep the file-based gate. There the gate reads only its own project's manifest, plus the workspace projects only when it links their commands.

The listing and stand-in building move into one function that both the install fast path and the gate use.
